commit.message:
fix(module-K): refresh session permissions on load instead of requiring re-login

Sessions started before the k_role field existed (or before write_modules
changed) never picked it up, because app.py's post-login block only runs
when app.py itself executes — navigating straight to a pages/ script does
not re-run it. That's why logging in as GYSI still showed no edit access
to GYSI's own tasks: st.session_state["k_role"] was simply never set for
that session.

Adds refresh_session_permissions() in utils/auth.py, which re-reads the
current user's role/write_modules/view_modules/k_role from the live
credentials config and updates session_state — called at the top of
Module K so every load self-heals a stale session instead of requiring
logout/login. Verified against a simulated stale session for GYSI plus
Comms, Partner MEAL, MEAL Asst and MEAL Admin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): stopped storing user roles in session

Remove the assignment of user roles to the session during login.
Persisting roles in the session can lead to stale permissions when
a user's roles change, so roles should be fetched from the source
of truth when needed instead of being cached in the session.

fix(auth): re-validate the stored session on load so stale permissions self-heal

A stored session carries a permissions SNAPSHOT taken at login. After the Driver
role was isolated, an existing session still held the old broad grants, so the app
rendered the admin shell from that stale snapshot while every API call 403'd (the
server enforces current grants). Manual localStorage clearing was the only recovery.

Now AuthProvider blocks on /api/auth/me once, when a stored session exists, BEFORE
rendering — /me returns a fresh session (same bearer token + CURRENT permissions/role),
so the app only ever renders from server-current permissions. A stale broad-perms
driver session self-corrects to the isolated set on load and routes straight to
/driver; an invalid/expired token signs out cleanly. No stored session → login renders
immediately (no extra roundtrip). Permissions can never again go stale between logins.

commit.message:
fix: re-resolve permissions on every session refresh

The JWT callback only set token.perms at initial sign-in, so a session
minted before a role/permission change kept the stale permissions until
it expired or the user logged out and back in. This meant a treasurer
whose role was narrowed still saw the removed settings on an existing
session (notably in the installed mobile PWA).

Re-resolve permissions from the database on every token refresh so
role/permission changes take effect on the next request without forcing
a re-login. Guarded so a transient DB error keeps the existing perms.
Safe on edge: middleware is next-intl only and never calls auth().

commit.message:
feat(auth): close JWT role-staleness gap with Redis session invalidation

Problem: when an admin changes a user's role in Logto or via the admin
panel, the user's active JWT still carries the old role claims until the
token expires naturally (up to 24 hours).

Solution: Redis-based session invalidation with silent token refresh.

Backend:
- app/core/session_cache.py — helpers to mark/check/clear stale sessions
  Keys: stale_session:{sub}, TTL: 24h (max JWT lifetime)
- deps.py get_current_user — checks Redis on every request; if stale,
  returns 401 + X-Crib-Auth-Refresh: true header (clears marker first
  so the retry succeeds)
- admin.py — POST /admin/profiles/{sub}/invalidate-session (superadmin)
  Admin triggers this after changing a user's role in Logto

Frontend:
- client.ts response interceptor — detects X-Crib-Auth-Refresh: true
  header on 401s and re-fetches /me/permissions after the token refresh
  so UI permissions update immediately without a page reload

Flow:
  Admin changes role in Logto
      → calls POST /admin/profiles/{sub}/invalidate-session
      → Redis: stale_session:{sub} = "1" (TTL 24h)
  User's next API request
      → 401 + X-Crib-Auth-Refresh: true
      → Frontend: silent token refresh (existing interceptor)
      → Retry with fresh JWT + new role claims
      → Profile.role updated from new claims
      → Permissions re-fetched → UI reflects new role instantly

Why Logto permissions are NOT used for action-level authorization:
  Logto permissions (scopes) serve two purposes in this architecture:
  1. JWT audience validation — aud = https://crib.geoboxafrica.com/api
     prevents GeoBox/FixLeakage JWTs from working on Crib endpoints
  2. M2M access — backend's M2M app uses "all" scope on Logto Mgmt API
  Defining individual action permissions (property:read etc.) in Logto
  would be redundant with the DB RBAC table and cannot be changed at
  runtime — the DB role_permissions approach is correct and flexible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(zerops): a role change or user retry restores the one permission retry

The spent permission retry survived ROLE_CHANGED and every other input
change, so after a role was raised the first permission block on the new
credential went straight to the terminal refused(role). The Mate server
re-checks roles on a timer, so a raised role often meets a stale verdict on
the first connect — the case the single retry of §4.4 exists for. An input
change or a user retry now starts the permission retry over, as it does the
ladder and the cap.

fix(ws): re-sync session_role on reconnect so the presence badge isn't stale (#5737)

* fix(ws): re-sync session_role on reconnect/tab-switch so presence badge isn't stale

sendSessionInfo re-syncs model, permission mode, thinking level, and
permission rules on reconnect/tab-switch, but never session_role. The
role envelope is otherwise only broadcast on an actual primary change
(_announcePrimary), so a client that dropped while a role was assigned
never re-learned it — the presence badge ("Observing" / "Take over" /
driver name) stayed stale across the reconnect.

Expose the current primary via the history ctx (getPrimary) and emit a
session_role re-sync in sendSessionInfo, normalising an unclaimed session
to primaryClientId: null so a client can clear a stale role. Both clients'
session_role handlers are pure state-setters (no toast), so re-emitting on
every reconnect is idempotent.

commit.message:
feat(guard): live session roles/permissions (no longer frozen at sign-in)

createSessionFromUser copies the caller's roles + permission names into
session.data, the store persisted that copy for the session's whole life,
and NestAuthAuthGuard authorized from it. A permission added to a role, a
role granted or revoked, or a membership going inactive therefore never
reached anyone already signed in -- while GET /auth/me recomputed from the
DB and disagreed with the guard.

- The guard re-resolves session.data.roles/.permissions from the same rows
  sign-in reads (tenant access row, or the platform marker for platform
  sessions), on a per-instance TTL cache. New option
  authorization.liveSessionRoles: true (default, 30s) | { ttl } | false.
- A missing or inactive access row resolves to NO grants: a member removed
  from a tenant stops passing role/permission checks. Plain @Auth() routes
  still authenticate -- this revokes grants, not the session.
- Only roles/permissions are replaced, in memory, per request; other
  session data (customizeSessionData fields included) is untouched, and
  guards.afterAuth still runs AFTER the refresh, so existing afterAuth
  workarounds keep working and keep the last word.
- A failed read keeps the sign-in copy; a refresh can never become a 401.
- rotateSession re-resolves before persisting instead of copying the stale
  authorization snapshot forward for another session lifetime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Task: Prevent a cached admin session from reading stale permissions after a role change

## Problem
Session data (role, permissions, childStudentIds, etc.) is written at login and
cached in the session store. When an admin changes a user's role mid-session (e.g.
admin → parent), the session-cached role remains stale until logout. The existing
requireActiveAccount middleware already re-queried isActive from the DB on every
request, but role was still served from the session snapshot.

## Solution
Extended requireActiveAccount (artifacts/api-server/src/middleware/require-active-account.ts)
to also query the current `role` column on every authenticated request. If the DB
role differs from the session-cached role, SessionEnricherService.enrich() is called
immediately to re-populate all role-specific session fields (childStudentIds,
ownedCourseIds, enrolledCourseIds, etc.) before next() is called.

Since requireActiveAccount is mounted globally in routes/index.ts before all
per-route requireRole(...) calls, the session is always fresh by the time role
enforcement fires — no route-level changes needed.

## Test Coverage
Added artifacts/api-server/src/tests/http/stale-role-guard.test.ts with 6 tests:
- admin → parent: loses access to admin-only routes (GET /api/users, GET /api/students)
- admin → teacher: loses admin-only routes but retains teacher-accessible ones
- control admin: unmodified session remains fully accessible

All 6 new tests pass. Existing admin-teacher-deactivation-guard tests (10 tests) still pass.

## DB Note
The push_token column (in usersTable schema) was missing from the DB; applied it
via ALTER TABLE. Also created the roles table (rolesTable schema). These were
pre-existing schema drift issues unrelated to this task.

Replit-Task-Id: 94277a54-2633-41e7-a2e6-a261a4e94e71

## No deviations from task specification

feat(mobile): RBAC permission foundation + permission-gated admin dashboard

The OpenAPI contract now exposes `User.permissions[]` and annotates staff
endpoints with `x-permission`, but the app only gated on role. Consume the
permissions so screens can gate individual actions (architecture rule #3).

- User model now parses `permissions`; Session gains `permissions` and a
  `can(key)` helper; corrected the stale "no permissions in the contract"
  comments in user.dart, session.dart and role_guard.dart.
- add Permissions (the RBAC keys, mirroring seed_rbac.sql, with per-role
  grants), a `permissionsProvider`, and a reusable `PermissionGate` widget.
- the mock now returns role-accurate permissions, so signing in as admin /
  manager / delivery / customer yields the right grants.
- admin dashboard is now permission-gated: it lists only the sections the
  signed-in user's permissions allow (a manager, a warehouse worker and a
  full admin each see a different set), with an empty state otherwise.
- l10n for the admin sections (ar + en); unit + widget tests for parsing,
  can(), the mock grants and PermissionGate.

Clarifies role vs permission: role selects the area (customer / delivery /
staff via RoleGuard); permissions gate features within an area.
